name: Chin filler

card.summary: Injectable filler (usually hyaluronic acid) placed at the chin to add projection or length without surgery; temporary, with rare but serious vascular complications.
card.aka: Chin augmentation with filler, liquid genioplasty
card.note: Rare vascular occlusion and tissue necrosis are documented; self-injection by forum users is outside any regulated setting.

quick.overview:
Chin filler is a non-surgical way to add volume to the chin, most often with hyaluronic acid gel injected by a clinician. Companies have run registered trials of several products specifically for chin retrusion, and published case reviews describe its use for reshaping the facial profile.

On looksmax.org it is discussed as a trial run before surgery or a temporary alternative to implants and genioplasty. Forum members also post self-injection accounts, which clinicians regard as outside normal safety conditions.
quick.mechanism: Hyaluronic acid or similar gel is injected near the bone to add volume, projecting or lengthening the chin. The effect lasts as long as the material persists in the tissue and is reversible with hyaluronidase for hyaluronic acid products.
quick.risks: The chin is generally regarded as a lower-risk injection area, but case reports describe vascular occlusion, skin necrosis and even tongue necrosis after chin filler. Anatomical studies map the arteries to inform safer injection. Fillers are regulated medical devices administered by licensed practitioners.

lead: Chin filler is a non-surgical cosmetic treatment in which an injectable gel, typically hyaluronic acid, is placed in the chin to increase its projection, height or contour. It is sometimes called a liquid genioplasty and is used both for age-related volume loss and for congenital chin retrusion. [1][3]

Published work includes a case review of 83 patients treated with combined forehead, nose and chin filler to alter the profile [1], and manufacturers have registered several trials of specific hyaluronic acid products for chin retrusion. [4][5][6] The literature also documents rare serious complications, including vascular occlusion and tongue necrosis. [2][7]

In looksmaxxing communities chin filler is discussed as a reversible, lower-cost alternative or precursor to chin implants and sliding genioplasty. Forum members also post accounts of self-injection; clinical literature on safety concerns the anatomy and complications of professional injection. [3][8][9]

paras: The filler is deposited in or near the chin's soft tissue and over the bone to move the soft-tissue pogonion forward or lengthen the chin. An encyclopedic summary of chin surgery lists hyaluronic acid and calcium hydroxyapatite as temporary fillers and notes that permanent silicone fillers have fallen out of favour because of migration and infection risks. [10]
A published technique paper describes a multilayered cannula approach to the chin, and a case series proposes a profile algorithm combining forehead, nose, lip and chin filler. [1][11]
A study using three-dimensional tomography and cadaveric dissection of 40 heads examined chin anatomy to discuss the avoidance of intravascular embolization. [3]

A case series reported unilateral tongue necrosis from vascular occlusion after hyaluronic acid chin augmentation, stating that chin filler is considered a safe injection area and that this complication is rare. [2] A 2026 case report describes vascular occlusion after a low-volume chin injection managed with pulsed hyaluronidase. [7]

Forum members ask whether chin filler would improve their profile, post transformation photographs, and discuss it alongside jaw filler. [8][9][12] Some threads document members injecting themselves or friends [16]; the wiki does not reproduce such instructions, and published literature on complications concerns professional administration. [2][3]
A case review of 83 consecutive patients treated with forehead, nose and chin filler assessed profile measurements and complications. [1]

Registered trials for chin products include Restylane Lyft with lidocaine (NCT05777759, n=175), Restylane Defyne (NCT03624816, n=140), a new dermal filler for chin correction (NCT04631263, n=140), Stylage XXL in Chinese adults (NCT05009381, n=174), Restylane Shaype versus Juvederm Volux (NCT06336772, n=40), and a phase 4 evaluation recruiting in 2026 (NCT07777926). [4][5][6][13][14][15]

timeline.event: A case review of combined forehead, nose and chin filler is published in the Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology. [1]
A tongue-necrosis case series and a cadaveric anatomy study of the chin are published. [2][3]

lore.intro: Members of looksmax.org discuss chin filler as a temporary, reversible way to test or improve chin projection, and some post self-injection results. [8][9][12]

claims.claim: Chin filler can approximate the look of surgery without surgery
claims.believers: Posters share before-and-after photographs and say filler added visible projection and helped them judge whether to pursue an implant or genioplasty. [9][12]
claims.experts: Manufacturer-registered trials have studied filler for chin retrusion, and a case review reported profile changes, but the volume added is smaller than what bone surgery can achieve according to surgical summaries. [1][4][10]

claims.claim: The chin is a safe area to inject
claims.believers: Members of self-injection threads describe chin filler as a procedure they performed on themselves or friends and report it as a success. [16]
claims.experts: Authors of case series state the chin is considered safe but report rare vascular occlusion, necrosis and tongue necrosis; an anatomical study maps vessels to reduce embolization risk. [2][3][7]

claims.claim: Self-injected chin filler gives results comparable to a clinic
claims.believers: Some members post self-administered results with photographs and say they were satisfied. [16]
claims.experts: No published study has evaluated self-administered chin filler; the safety literature concerns anatomy and complications in clinical practice. [2][3]
